changelog: Fix: 2026_09_17_0002 (v3.12.0) ran correctly — all 41 inserts and 17 updates landed — but its own post-verify guard failed because live had drifted further than the guard anticipated. Trade 80 (BNBUSDT, 2026-09-14) was a genuine trade logged after the snapshot the migration's id mapping was built from, pushing the challenge's real row/loss counts from 58/35 to 59/36 and tripping the guard's hardcoded COUNT(*)=58 check. Trade 79 (ZECUSDT Long), also logged after the snapshot, turned out to be the same closed position as CSV row n=1 — but 0002's duplicate check matched on an exact (pair, direction, time_in), and a 9-second gap between trade 79's hand-typed time_in and Bitfunded's own defeated it, so 0002 inserted a second row for the same position instead of recognizing trade 79 as already covering it

Fix: 2026_09_17_0003 updates trade 79 to Bitfunded's own price/time/pnl for CSV row n=1 (same treatment the original 17 matched rows got in 0002), deletes the duplicate row 0002 inserted (confirmed to have zero trade_variables before deletion — trade 79's 9 rows were never touched), and re-scans the whole challenge with a 5-minute tolerance window instead of an exact timestamp to confirm no second undiscovered near-duplicate exists

Process: 2026_09_17_0002 was not edited (checksum-locked once applied) — 0003 instead records it directly in schema_migrations as 'applied', since its data changes were correct and retrying it would fail the same stale COUNT(*)=58 check forever now that the challenge legitimately holds 59 rows

Process: added a migration checklist note — any future bulk-import migration that dedupes against existing rows must match on (pair, direction) plus a tolerance window on time_in (this codebase now uses +/-5 minutes), never an exact timestamp, since a broker's own execution time and a trader's hand-typed entry for the same fill routinely differ by seconds to minutes
